```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
library(OECDscaleup)
d <- variable_dictionary[variable_dictionary$dataset == "trade_RAW", ]
blank <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", x)
```

OECD project on SME scaling up. For information: scaleup@oecd.org,
juergen.amann@oecd.org.

The trade package
(`run_trade_pipeline()`) adds
firm-level international trade in goods to the scale-up indicators. It
reads the same `base_financials_<CT>.dta` (and, if present,
`plants_RAW_<CT>.dta`, `tl3_typology.dta`, `exchange_rates.dta`) as the
scale-up pipeline, described in `vignette("input-data")`, plus one trade
file. The same information is in the package dataset `variable_dictionary`
(`?variable_dictionary`).

## File

`trade_RAW_<CT>.dta` in `config$input_dir`, where `<CT>` is the two-letter
country code given to `config_scaleup()`. It holds transaction-level
international trade in goods statistics (ITGS): one row per firm, year,
flow (import or export), destination country and 8-digit CN product.

## General rules

1. **Missing values** are coded `.` in numeric variables and `"."` in
   string variables. The package also reads an empty string as missing.
2. **`trade_value` is in EUR thousand.** Values in euros are declared with
   `config_scaleup(trade_value_unit = "EUR")`, and the build divides them by
   1000. (For PT and HU, which delivered euros in earlier rounds, `"EUR"` is
   the default.)
3. Definitions follow the Eurostat (2022) *European business statistics
   compilers' manual for international trade in goods statistics, detailed
   data*:
   <https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-manuals-and-guidelines/-/ks-gq-22-008>.

## Priorities

All the variables of `trade_RAW` are must-have: the trade build stops if
one is missing.

## What to supply

```{r}
coding <- ifelse(d$coding == "", d$format, paste0(d$format, "; ", d$coding))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Variable = paste0("`", d$variable, "`"), Priority = d$priority, Definition = d$definition,
  `Format and coding` = coding, Source = d$source, Notes = blank(d$notes), check.names = FALSE
))
```

## What the package does with it

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Variable = paste0("`", d$variable, "`"), `The package needs it` = d$package_requirement,
  `What the package does with it` = d$package_use, check.names = FALSE
))
```

The trade build (`build_trade_panel()`
and `build_trade_accounts_indicators()`)
collapses the transactions to one row per firm and year and merges them onto
`base_financials`:

* `exp_value`, `imp_value`: total exports and imports (EUR thousand);
  `exporter`, `importer`: 1 for a positive value;
* `exp_all_partners`, `exp_eu_partners`: number of export destinations, all
  and in the EU;
* `exp_products`, `imp_products`: number of 6-digit products;
  `exp_core_prod`, `imp_core_prod`: share of the largest product;
* `y4_exporter`: first-time exporters over t-3 to t;
* `HGX10`, `HGX20`, `HGNX10`, `HGNX20`: turnover scalers whose export
  growth is at least (heavy exporting) or less than (light exporting) half
  the turnover growth that makes a high-growth firm;
* `sector_exporter`, `digit_sect`: sector group by export status, and by
  the digital intensity of the industry.

Import partner countries are not part of the data, so there are no import
partner counts.
